title: Privacy campaigners to ask court to ban sale of Meta AI glasses
key_facts: Two Dutch privacy organisations, Offlimits and The Firewall, are seeking an injunction against Meta to ban sales of its AI glasses in the Netherlands.
They argue the glasses, which let users film what they see, breach Dutch criminal laws protecting people from being filmed without consent.
Lawyers wrote to Meta two weeks ago demanding it withdraw the glasses or face legal action; the deadline passed without a response.
Several thousand pairs have been bought in the Netherlands since opticians began selling them a year ago; more than seven million pairs have been sold worldwide.
Several Dutch music venues banned the devices after a man was caught filming women near toilets at a festival in August.
They say the LED recording light is not always visible and can be covered, and that Meta stores footage and uses it to train its AI, which they argue is also an offence.
Robbert Hoving, managing director of Offlimits, said: "We are drawing a line"; the groups hope the court will announce a hearing date by the end of the week.
DutchNews has asked Meta for comment.

why_it_matters_hint: Dutch campaigners want a court to stop sales of camera glasses they say let people be filmed in private places without consent.
event_date: Mid-Oct 2026 (the letter of formal notice was sent about two weeks earlier)
notes: Single-source; Meta has not commented. The legal claims are the campaigners'. Follows our 3 Oct and 5 Oct 2026 editions on Dutch retailers pausing sales and Norway's proposed ban.
